message.content:
Hydrogen is the simplest and most abundant element in the universe, and it has several key properties that make it unique:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 (one proton) |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (mostly protium, ^1H) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Common isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H), Tritium (^3H) |
| **Physical state at STP** | Gas (colorless, odorless, tasteless) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.8 °C (20.27 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g/L at 0 °C, 1 atm |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (first ionization) |
| **Bond dissociation energy** | H₂ → 2 H: 436 kJ/mol |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water vapor (combustion) |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals; forms covalent bonds in organic molecules |
| **Abundance** | ~75 % of all atoms in the observable universe |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis, petroleum refining), laboratory standard gas, cryogenic coolant, etc. |

These properties cover its basic atomic characteristics, physical behavior, chemical reactivity, and practical applications.
